purpose: Which range Word gives a bookmark name that a document repeats, and which range a REF field naming it resolves to after a field update, compared with ECMA-376 Part 1 § 17.13.6.2, whose name attribute says the first bookmark in document order shall be maintained and later ones should be ignored (#1264).
procedure: Each `bodyXml` was packaged with `buildDocxFromBodyXml` (packages/docx-core/src/testing/ooxml-fixtures.ts), so no other part names a bookmark. Each REF field was written with the cached result `stale`. The DOCX was staged in Word's sandbox container and opened in the background, and then, through AppleScript bound to that document by name: the name and text of every member of its `bookmarks` collection were read, `update field` ran on every field, each field's code and result were read, and the document was closed without saving. The `repeatedNames` run was made twice with identical output.
finding: Word keeps one bookmark per repeated name, and it is the last range in document order, not the first: `Target` names the second of its two ranges, and `Probe`, repeated three times with descending w:id values, names the third. A REF field resolves to that last range after a field update. Word compares names without regard to case: `Other` and `OTHER` become one bookmark named `OTHER` holding the later range, and both `REF OTHER` and `REF other` resolve to it. Word therefore does not follow the § 17.13.6.2 sentence about repeated names, and the spec and Word disagree about which range a repeated name denotes.
